status.en: 179 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 28% fewer than the week before, most of them in Abuja, Plateau State and Lagos.
status.nb: 179 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 28 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Abuja, Plateau State og Lagos.

summary.en: Bandits continue to target civilians and security forces, killing traders and an immigration officer in Niger and ambushing a convoy in Zamfara, while Fulani militias have hacked and killed Christians in Benue and carried out attacks in Plateau and Niger. Kidnappers have abducted a couple and their infant in Kaduna, prompting Atiku Abubakar to call for their rescue. ISWAP fighters launched an assault on a town in Borno but were repelled after air strikes killed dozens of militants. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Banditter fortsetter å angripe sivile og sikkerhetsstyrker, dreper handelsmenn og en immigrasjonsoffiser i Niger og overfaller en konvoi i Zamfara, mens Fulani-milits har hacket og drept kristne i Benue og utført angrep i Plateau og Niger. Kidnapperne har bortført et par og deres spedbarn i Kaduna, noe som fikk Atiku Abubakar til å kreve deres redning. ISWAP-krigere lanserte et angrep på en by i Borno, men ble avverget etter luftangrep som drepte dusinvis av militante. Konflikten førte til 1 486 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
